name: BD-JB2 - BDJO baseDirectory path traversal in BdjPolicyImpl

root_cause.summary: BD-J decides whether a JAR gets AllPermission with a prefix test in com.sony.bdjstack.security.BdjPolicyImpl: a code source whose file path starts with $JAVA_HOME/lib/ext is trusted. The Xlet location comes from the BDJO baseDirectory, and a value such as file:///app0/cdc/lib/../../../disc/BDMV/JAR/00000.jar passes the prefix test after the runtime resolves the relative components, so an external JAR on the disc is treated as a trusted $JAVA_HOME/lib JAR. The Xlet then loads with AllPermission, disables the SecurityManager and reaches native code.
root_cause.primitive: path traversal / missing canonicalization in the BD-J policy check, leading to AllPermission on an attacker-controlled JAR
root_cause.trigger: crafted bdjo.xml/BDJO with a file:// baseDirectory containing ../ on a burned Blu-ray
root_cause.consequence: JAR loads with AllPermission and the Xlet escapes the Java sandbox to native userland code execution

discovery_approach.summary: TheFloW found the path-validation bug before 2023-09-11 while reviewing the BD-J stack, reported it to Sony on 2023-09-22 and disclosed it on 2023-10-25. It was a replacement for the original userprefs deserialization gadget: instead of a serialized file it abuses the BDJO baseDirectory so an external JAR is treated as a $JAVA_HOME/lib JAR. Gezine later confirmed the primitive still worked through PS4 12.52 and chained it with BD-JB3.
signals: BdjPolicyImpl.getPermissions comparing location.getFile() against javaHome + "lib" + File.separator + "ext" with startsWith
a file:// URL containing ../ that resolves outside $JAVA_HOME/lib
no canonical-path normalization before the permission decision

differences: The fix is in BD-J path validation: 13.00/8.00 no longer grant AllPermission to a JAR reached through the BDJO baseDirectory traversal (PS4/PS5 wiki).

PS4 kept the same class of primitive alive with JAR-infix variants through 12.52 (/lib/ext/sunjce_provider.jar and /bdjstack/lib/ext), and 13.00-13.02 used BD-JB-13.00 (CVE-2025-64390); PS5 8.00 closed BD-JB2 and later needed BD-JB-13.42 for 13.42 and below.

patch_evidence.what: the PS4 and PS5 dev wikis record the vulnerable prefix check, the affected ranges and the fix releases (PS4 13.00 / PS5 8.00); no binary diff is public
patch_evidence.limits: no firmware bytes, no Sony advisory text and no patched decompilation are stored or linked here

sources.supports: BD-JB2 at PS4 <=12.52, the BdjPolicyImpl prefix bug and the baseDirectory traversal, fix in PS4 13.00, and the BD-JB3.2/BD-JB-13.00 variants
PS5 BD-JB2 at <=7.61 and fixed in PS5 8.00
public bd-jb implementation repository that the BD-JB2 writeup is based on
BD-JB discs working on PS4 9.00-12.52 and the 13.00+ workaround that copies 00000.jar into bdjstack/lib/ext
the privileged URLClassLoader example with file:///app0/bdjstack/lib/ext/../../../../disc/BDMV/JAR/00000.jar, which is the same traversal primitive

gaps: No binary diff of the 13.00/8.00 fix; the wikis state the affected/fixed versions and the prefix-check mechanism but do not quote the patched code.
The PS4 wiki says 13.00-13.02 was still exploitable via BD-JB-13.00 (CVE-2025-64390), so 'fixed in 13.00' applies to BD-JB2 specifically, not to every BD-J path trick.
The exact BDJO XML field order and the runtime's path-normalization order are described by the wiki, not by a vendor advisory.

entry_chain.stage: Burned Blu-ray inserted; the player parses /disc/BDMV/BDJO/00000.bdjo and resolves the Xlet location
entry_chain.image_visible: BDMV/BDJO descriptors and the JAR are on the disc; the BD-J stack classes are in system_ex, not the kernel image
entry_chain.runtime_only: which BDJO the player selects and how it normalizes the file:// URL

entry_chain.image_visible: the literal baseDirectory string in bdjo.xml; the BdjPolicyImpl prefix check in bdjstack.jar
entry_chain.runtime_only: whether the resolved code source still starts with $JAVA_HOME/lib/ext when the permission decision is made

entry_chain.stage: The JAR is treated as a trusted $JAVA_HOME/lib JAR and receives AllPermission
entry_chain.image_visible: the startsWith test in BdjPolicyImpl.getPermissions; no kernel-image signal
entry_chain.runtime_only: the actual ProtectionDomain and permission collection attached to the Xlet

entry_chain.stage: SecurityManager disabled and native code reached through Unsafe/findEntry/setcontext
entry_chain.image_visible: Unsafe and NativeLibrary references in the BD-J runtime; no kernel-image signal
entry_chain.runtime_only: symbol resolution and the native call primitive

entry_chain.stage: Chain to the firmware's kernel exploit (AIO double free on PS5 <=10.01, umtx on PS5 <=7.61, Lapse on PS4)
entry_chain.image_visible: the kernel image contains the candidate bug sites; the chosen exploit depends on the firmware
entry_chain.runtime_only: the actual kernel version, offsets and heap state
